body:
Thanks for the #678 update. We have an intake owner for the 85 reported bounds and will retain the new witnesses for independent checks. One n260 provenance link needs clarification before we can carry the intermediate bound and seed credit into the record.

At `c6da0fc`, `upper_bounds.json` gives the preceding n260 side `4161444696515435316429350771309/250000000000000000000000000000` with decompressed SHA-256 `e90993b1c0f625d1d6c2d1ea3b5f391bfe6d98f5bc387a10863434bb9db4934e`. The retained `certificates/best/manifest.json` and `certificates/n260.json` at that same revision instead point to the earlier T-196 witness (`df90e58d702555c8487a93f34b023f43903cb116c42ed50623d429dba2252d31`). The new `certificates/n260.json` names the `e90993...` seed as `evand/search/regularize/lists/certs/n-260.cert.gz`, but that path at the Evan revision pinned in `bound_sources.json` (`0f37f49fa521f411d8e35c82f746e679b3447e46`) decompresses to a different header and SHA-256 (`0f8bc736897812b792a787bfe45277b4a90943147ff522c1df44e8244925ef07`).

Could you provide the immutable source revision/path or exact bytes for the `e90993...` seed, and confirm its attribution? This is a question about the preceding bound and seed custody; it does not judge the feasibility of the new #678 n260 witness. We have not independently replayed the new certificates yet.

Thanks. The mismatch comes from two errors on our side. The seed itself is intact.

**1. `e90993…` is the SHA-256 of the gzip file, not the decompressed text.** Our importer hashes the `.cert.gz` bytes as stored, and none of our records said so. The decompressed SHA-256 of the same file is `34b203dd126640c533f2ab88b5af8d593db8bf60a8f3d3527defd9cac85c6d40`.

**2. Our evand pin was stale.** `bound_sources.json` has pinned `0f37f49` since before af8cb79. The checkout we imported from had already been fetched past the commit that introduced these bytes. At `0f37f49` the path still holds the older regularized register packing, which is what you found. Its side is `8328427124746190097686661719667/500000000000000000000000000000` (11 + 4√2 ≈ 16.656854249492), with gzip SHA-256 `2ea51d9aa1073b7a761afc1988216a2046ded48392b558c5bc0cd846216da1e6` and decompressed SHA-256 `0f8bc736…`.

### Immutable source for the seed

- Repository: `evand/square-packing`
- Commit: [`14a9af8be4a8b8a8328c3eb6b486a2e553380193`](https://github.com/evand/square-packing/blob/14a9af8be4a8b8a8328c3eb6b486a2e553380193/search/regularize/lists/certs/n-260.cert.gz) (2026-10-17T17:25:17Z, "Site up to date: 28 newer records regularized…")
- Path: `search/regularize/lists/certs/n-260.cert.gz`
- gzip SHA-256: `e90993b1c0f625d1d6c2d1ea3b5f391bfe6d98f5bc387a10863434bb9db4934e`
- Decompressed SHA-256: `34b203dd126640c533f2ab88b5af8d593db8bf60a8f3d3527defd9cac85c6d40`
- Header: `260 4161444696515435316429350771309/250000000000000000000000000000`

GitHub's history for that path shows two commits: `346c6ed` (Oct 10, the `0f8bc736` version) and `14a9af8`. The bytes are unchanged through current `main` (`ddf09e3`). I fetched the file from GitHub at `0f37f49`, `14a9af8` and `main` and hashed each copy. The decompressed `14a9af8` file passes our `verify_bound_certificate.py` with both the closed and strict verdicts true.

### Attribution

The file is Evan Daniel's exact-form solve of Joost de Winter's #668 packing. It is the analytic optimum of that packing, about 1.8e-8 below de Winter's posted side `16645778804181379786535601/1000000000000000000000000` (`df90e58d…`). Evan credits de Winter for it in three places: [TODO.md L46](https://github.com/evand/square-packing/blob/ddf09e382ab3c63675476503d51d1a405bb2f7e6/TODO.md#L46) ("the analytic optimum of de Winter's #668 packing … credit de Winter"), [credits-review.md L1564](https://github.com/evand/square-packing/blob/ddf09e382ab3c63675476503d51d1a405bb2f7e6/site/notes/credits-review.md#L1564) and [PACKER.md L4011](https://github.com/evand/square-packing/blob/ddf09e382ab3c63675476503d51d1a405bb2f7e6/search/packer/PACKER.md#L4011).

We also compared the two packings ourselves. After a 180° rotation, 240 of the 260 squares coincide with `df90e58d…` to within 1e-8. The other 20 are axis-aligned wall squares shifted along the wall, which comes from Evan's display regularization. So the construction credit belongs to **Joost de Winter (#668)**, and the exact-form certificate is **Evan Daniel's**. Our records named only de Winter. We'll add Evan as the certificate source.

### Why c6da0fc disagreed with itself

At c6da0fc, `upper_bounds.json` took the n260 side from our external-certificate index, where the entry was still marked pending. `certificates/n260.cert` and the manifest list only bytes we keep in our repo, and for n260 those were de Winter's `df90e58d…`. The `e90993…` bytes were never copied into our repo, so that index cited a bound whose witness was only upstream.

### Seed custody for the #678 witness

Our importer converts the best external certificate to a float seed. Rerunning that conversion on the `14a9af8` file reproduces the seed's SHA-256 byte for byte: `9fdc6b41b93f2f52b991a6bc56b9423837336b51e519f5932b03369f86625cd8`. The search chain from that seed is:

| Job | Input SHA-256 | Output side | Output SHA-256 |
|---:|---|---:|---|
| 109310 | `9fdc6b41b93f2f52b991a6bc56b9423837336b51e519f5932b03369f86625cd8` (seed from `14a9af8`) | 16.645758822386 | `6e442bbe2845383fa02d364db0fe4eeec5f81f2f25a6df6c369b7347a4245503` |
| 109500 | `6e442bbe2845383fa02d364db0fe4eeec5f81f2f25a6df6c369b7347a4245503` | 16.645754570563 | `3c86835ac3fd72f3ead9dd5ad1a7ed687dfacb3ab23268493ff8065e455405d8` |
| 109690 | `3c86835ac3fd72f3ead9dd5ad1a7ed687dfacb3ab23268493ff8065e455405d8` | 16.645753250529 | `da29d67ec186684b9690ab3a55289093ed53d9b2461979cfbd63b9e19fd1887e` |

The job 109690 output became `certificates/n260.cert` (`635dbf25a2550f22e4259a850da1ad02f2762527a367d90193458fa644d12908`). The intermediate float files are not in the repository; I can attach them if that helps.

We'll push a follow-up that refreshes the evand pin, labels each external hash as gzip or decompressed, and adds Evan Daniel's certificate credit. I'll link the commit here.

Thanks for the precise revision and hash-kind correction. We fetched the 4,112-byte gzip at `evand/square-packing` commit `14a9af8be4a8b8a8328c3eb6b486a2e553380193`, path `search/regularize/lists/certs/n-260.cert.gz`, and independently confirmed both bindings:

- gzip SHA-256: `e90993b1c0f625d1d6c2d1ea3b5f391bfe6d98f5bc387a10863434bb9db4934e`;
- decompressed SHA-256: `34b203dd126640c533f2ab88b5af8d593db8bf60a8f3d3527defd9cac85c6d40`.

The first non-comment header also matches `260 4161444696515435316429350771309/250000000000000000000000000000`. This resolves the immutable-source and hash-kind question for those seed bytes. Our earlier comment incorrectly called `e90993…` a decompressed hash.

The intake will retain your distinction between Joost de Winter’s construction credit (#668) and Evan Daniel’s exact-form certificate source. The already merged T-196 remains the earlier submitted witness; a later seed or refinement does not rewrite that chronology.

This check establishes data custody only. We have not independently verified the float conversion or intermediate search chain, packing identity, the asserted analytic optimum, or feasibility of the 85 new submitted bounds. Those checks remain separate intake work. Please link the promised source-pin, hash-kind and credit correction when it is available; intermediate float files can remain a separate provenance attachment rather than a prerequisite for identifying this exact seed.
